svg.text: The Go installer sets up the developer's own shell
Scenario: On a machine without which, the Go installer links /usr/local/go to the Go it installed

g.text: Given a developer with sudo is on a machine without which and without Go
A fresh Ubuntu machine with no which command, as on a base Arch Linux install, and no Go. The

text.tspan: type which go; sudo -n true && echo "sudo works"

g.text: Then the Go installer links /usr/local/go to the Go it installed, and Go's standard library
The developer runs the Go installer, the same line task dev:setup-environment runs. With sudo it runs again as root,
installs Go with apt-get and says where Go lives, then links /usr/local/go there.
readlink shows where /usr/local/go points, and ls finds Go's standard library under it, in src/runtime: a tool that sets
GOROOT to /usr/local/go builds with the Go that was installed.
